relations.subject: P. V. Kane
relations.evidence: I was transferred at my own request to the Elphinstone High School in Bombay as 5th assistant on Rs. 75 in April 1907. ... I was made Head Sanskrit teacher

relations.subject: P. V. Kane
relations.evidence: I was appointed to act as Professor of Sanskrit at the Elphinstone College from February to April 1909 in place of Prof. S. R. Bhandarkar

relations.subject: S. R. Bhandarkar
relations.evidence: in place of Prof. S. R. Bhandarkar who had been deputed on some Govt. work.

relations.subject: P. V. Kane
relations.evidence: In 1916 I worked as Honorary Professor of Sanskrit at the Wilson College, when Prof. S R Bhandarkar, who was permanent Professor, fell ill

relations.subject: S. R. Bhandarkar
relations.evidence: when Prof. S R Bhandarkar, who was permanent Professor, fell ill

relations.subject: P. V. Kane
relations.evidence: In 1917 June I was appointed as a Professor of Law in the Govt. Law College at Bombay. ... I was Professor of Law for six years (1917-1923).

relations.subject: P. V. Kane
relations.evidence: Dr. Belvalkar, Dr. Gune and several others supported the idea and about thirty people including myself contributed Rs. 500 each for the purchase of a big vacant plot of 30 acres in Poona and, after setting aside nearly half of the purchased plot for the Institute to be named after Dr. R. G. Bhandarkar
